- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates near-term price support or volatility.
- Forecasts often lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the horizon (days 10–20), indicating delayed reaction to recent price movements.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility — e.g., after a spike, forecast jumps higher than true outcome, then drops too fast, missing intermediate support levels.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to smoothly transition from high to low prices, instead showing abrupt drops or plateaus.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days, suggesting model overweights short-term momentum or ignores seasonal/structural constraints.
